message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"db0d546892478834f06c7b48c50b869dc42fe667060e2a82a3b15fd8435aaff1","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:59","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","units":[{"unit_id":"sec01-u01","module_id":"sec01-m01","objective_ids":["sec01-u01"],"title":{"text":"Who needs an Alabama license","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Knowing when a license or a new exam is required keeps you from driving illegally after a move or a lapse.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]},{"text":"The exemptions have different time limits, and mixing them up can leave a newcomer or visitor unlicensed.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-R06"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Dana moves to Alabama with a valid license from her previous state and keeps driving for two months.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A new resident may drive on the previous state's license for only thirty days after moving in.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R06"]},"result":{"text":"After thirty days Dana needs an Alabama license, so her last month of driving was outside the rule.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F01"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a new resident gets the same ninety days a year that some visitors get.","fact_ids":["sec01-R06"]},"correction":{"text":"The ninety-day yearly limit is for visitors from countries that do not license drivers; new residents get thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-R06"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Newcomers thirty, visitors ninety.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F05","sec01-R06"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A friend moved to Alabama three weeks ago with a valid license from her previous state. May she still drive on it?","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R06"]},"answer":{"text":"Yes, because a new resident may use it for thirty days after moving.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},"rationale":{"text":"Three weeks is inside the thirty-day new resident window, which is separate from the ninety-day visitor limit.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R06"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Who must hold a license","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Every resident driver needs one.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]},{"text":"A few drivers are exempt for now.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson opens the section on license requirements and identification. Before you think about tests and paperwork, you need to know who must hold an Alabama driver license in the first place. The short answer is that every Alabama resident who drives a motor vehicle needs one. Then come the details: when an expired license sends you back to the driver exam, and the short list of people who may drive without an Alabama license for a while. Several of these rules carry different time limits, so pay close attention to which number goes with which driver. Those numbers are where most mix-ups happen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The license rule and the exam","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Residents who drive need a license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07"]},{"text":"Farm tractor moves are the exception.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07"]},{"text":"Never licensed here means an exam.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every Alabama resident who drives a motor vehicle needs a driver license. The one exception in this rule is temporarily moving a farm tractor or an implement of husbandry along a road. Next, the driver exam. If you have never been licensed in Alabama, you must pass it. If your Alabama license expired more than three years ago, you must pass it again. A license from another state works on a shorter clock: if it expired one year or less ago, no exam is needed. So the cutoff is three years for an expired Alabama license, but one year for an expired out-of-state license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Drivers with another license","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Federal employees in government vehicles.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F07"]},{"text":"Residents sixteen plus with a home license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F07"]},{"text":"Non-resident full-time students.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Some drivers may skip the Alabama license. A federal employee driving a vehicle owned or leased by the United States government needs no Alabama license for that driving. A resident aged sixteen or older who carries a valid license from a home state or home country may drive without an Alabama one, and that includes out-of-state military families stationed here on long assignments. A non-resident who is a full-time student at an Alabama school, college or trade school may also drive on a valid home license. Each of these exemptions depends on a specific condition, such as the vehicle, the license held, or full-time enrollment.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Visitors and new residents","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Non-licensing country visitor: ninety days a year.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F06"]},{"text":"Home registration must be current.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F06"]},{"text":"New resident: thirty days after moving.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Two exemptions come with clocks. First, a non-resident aged sixteen or older from a country that does not license drivers may drive here for up to ninety days in a calendar year, as long as the vehicle is registered for the current year in the home country. Second, a new resident who holds a valid license from the previous state may drive on it for thirty days after moving to Alabama. Take the worked example of Dana, who moves here and keeps driving on her old license for two months. Thirty days was her limit, so after that she needed an Alabama license to stay within the rule.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Thirty days versus ninety","fact_ids":["sec01-R06","sec01-R07","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"New resident: thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec01-R06","sec01-R07","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-F02"]},{"text":"Visitor from non-licensing country: ninety a year.","fact_ids":["sec01-R06","sec01-R07","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-F02"]},{"text":"Different drivers, different clocks.","fact_ids":["sec01-R06","sec01-R07","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a common trap. Learners hear the ninety-day limit for visitors and assume a new resident gets the same time. That is not the rule. The ninety days per calendar year belong to visitors from countries that do not license drivers. A person who has moved to Alabama and become a resident gets only thirty days on the previous state's license. A second trap sits in the exam cutoffs: an expired Alabama license sends you back to the exam after more than three years, but an expired out-of-state license does so after more than one year. When a question gives you a number, first decide which kind of driver it describes.","fact_ids":["sec01-R06","sec01-R07","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the newcomer window","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R06","sec01-F05","sec01-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Moved here three weeks ago.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R06","sec01-F05","sec01-F01"]},{"text":"May she still use the old license?","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R06","sec01-F05","sec01-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a friend moved to Alabama three weeks ago, and she still carries a valid license from her previous state. May she keep driving on it? Settle on your answer first. Yes, she may, because a new resident can drive on the previous state's license for thirty days after moving, and three weeks is inside that window. Do not reach for the ninety-day figure here, because that yearly limit is for visitors from countries that do not license drivers. Once her thirty days pass, she will need an Alabama license, since every resident who drives must have one.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R06","sec01-F05","sec01-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"License basics recap","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-R06","sec01-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Every resident driver needs a license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-R06","sec01-F07"]},{"text":"Three years Alabama, one year elsewhere.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-R06","sec01-F07"]},{"text":"Thirty days newcomer, ninety days visitor.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-R06","sec01-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us sum up. Every Alabama resident who drives needs a license, except when temporarily moving a farm tractor or implement on a road. You must pass the driver exam if you were never licensed here or your Alabama license expired more than three years ago, while an out-of-state license expired one year or less needs none. Federal employees in government vehicles, residents sixteen or older with a valid home license, and non-resident full-time students may drive without an Alabama license. New residents get thirty days, and visitors from non-licensing countries get up to ninety days a year. Next, we look at who Alabama refuses to license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R07","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-R06","sec01-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u02","module_id":"sec01-m02","objective_ids":["sec01-u02"],"title":{"text":"Eligibility and the school rule","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Knowing the refusal reasons tells you whether an application can succeed before you visit a license office.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},{"text":"Young applicants must satisfy a school rule as well as the age rule, or the license is not issued.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-R10"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Sam is seventeen, has not graduated, and is still attending high school when he applies.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10"]},"reasoning":{"text":"He is over the minimum age of sixteen, and the under-nineteen rule calls for graduation or current attendance.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F10"]},"result":{"text":"Because he is attending school, he meets the rule, and he brings the signed student enrollment form as proof.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F21"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking that reaching sixteen is the only age rule for a license.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10"]},"correction":{"text":"Sixteen is the minimum age, but applicants under nineteen must also meet the school graduation or attendance rule.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F08","sec01-F10"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Sixteen to start, school until nineteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F10"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A seventeen-year-old who has stopped attending school applies for a license. Is being over sixteen enough?","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F10"]},"answer":{"text":"Not by itself, because applicants under nineteen must also meet the school rule.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F10"]},"rationale":{"text":"The minimum age is sixteen, but under nineteen the law also calls for graduation or current attendance, with limited exclusions.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-R10"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"When a license is refused","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Some applicants cannot be licensed.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"Young applicants face a school rule.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers who can and cannot get an Alabama license. Alabama turns away some applicants because of age, a record in another state, a failed exam, or a condition that makes safe control of a vehicle unlikely. Young applicants face one more requirement tied to school, and that rule comes with its own form. Finally, every person applying for an original Alabama license or ID card must prove they are allowed to be in the United States. Keep two different ages in mind as you go, because the minimum age and the school rule age are not the same, and test questions like to blur them together.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Reasons for refusal","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Under sixteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},{"text":"Suspended or revoked in any state.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},{"text":"Failed a required exam.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},{"text":"Addiction or disabling impairment.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Alabama will not license anyone under sixteen. It will not license anyone whose license is suspended or revoked in any state, not only Alabama. It will not license someone who fails a required exam. A license is also refused to a habitual drunkard or a narcotics addict. Finally, it is refused when a physical or mental impairment would keep the person from ordinary control of a vehicle, and the judgment on that belongs to ALEA or the examiner. Notice that a suspension anywhere counts, so moving to Alabama does not wipe away a suspension or revocation from another state. Each reason on this list blocks the license by itself.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The under-nineteen school rule","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F21"]},"lines":[{"text":"Applies to applicants under nineteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F21"]},{"text":"Graduation or current attendance.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F21"]},{"text":"Bring the signed enrollment form.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F21"]}],"narration":{"text":"Applicants under nineteen must meet Alabama Act ninety-three dash three sixty-eight. That law calls for graduation from secondary school or current attendance, with limited exclusions. The paperwork that proves it is the Student Enrollment or Exclusion Form, called form D L one ninety-three. Every applicant under nineteen must bring a current copy signed by authorized staff, and the form is available at schools or at license offices. Take Sam, who is seventeen and still attending high school. He is past the minimum age, he meets the attendance part of the rule, and his signed form proves it at the license office.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F21"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Sixteen is not the whole story","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F08","sec01-F10","sec01-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Minimum age: sixteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F08","sec01-F10","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"School rule: under nineteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F08","sec01-F10","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"Every original applicant proves presence.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F08","sec01-F10","sec01-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Many people believe that once you reach sixteen, age no longer matters. In fact there are two separate lines. Sixteen is the minimum licensing age. Nineteen is the line for the school rule: anyone under nineteen must also show graduation or current attendance under the Act, with limited exclusions. So a seventeen-year-old can be old enough and still be refused for failing the school rule. On top of both age rules, every applicant for an original Alabama license or ID card must prove authorized presence in the United States under federal law, whatever their age.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F08","sec01-F10","sec01-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the age rules","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F10","sec01-F21","sec01-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Seventeen, not attending school.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F10","sec01-F21","sec01-F08"]},{"text":"Is age sixteen enough?","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F10","sec01-F21","sec01-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a seventeen-year-old who has stopped attending school applies for an Alabama license. Is being over sixteen enough to qualify? Settle on your answer first. Not by itself. Sixteen is only the minimum age. Because this applicant is under nineteen, the school rule also applies, and it calls for secondary school graduation or current attendance, with limited exclusions. The applicant would also need the signed student enrollment form showing where things stand. Being old enough and meeting the school rule are two separate tests, and both must be satisfied.","fact_ids":["sec01-R10","sec01-F10","sec01-F21","sec01-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Eligibility recap","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F21","sec01-R10","sec01-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"No license under sixteen or while suspended.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F21","sec01-R10","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"Under nineteen, school rule applies.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F21","sec01-R10","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"Original applicants prove authorized presence.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F21","sec01-R10","sec01-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us sum up. Alabama refuses anyone under sixteen, anyone suspended or revoked in any state, and anyone who fails a required exam. It also refuses a habitual drunkard or narcotics addict, and anyone whose physical or mental impairment, in the view of ALEA or the examiner, would prevent ordinary control of a vehicle. Applicants under nineteen must also meet the school graduation or attendance rule, and they bring a current student enrollment form signed by authorized staff. Every applicant for an original license or ID card proves authorized presence. Next, we look at the identification documents you bring.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F21","sec01-R10","sec01-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u03","module_id":"sec01-m03","objective_ids":["sec01-u03"],"title":{"text":"Identification documents that count","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-R08","sec01-F13"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The wrong mix of documents sends you home from the license office without a license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-R08"]},{"text":"A document can be the right type and still be rejected if its condition or certification is wrong.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Lee brings a certified birth certificate and a marriage license, and neither one has a photo.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F22","sec01-F24"]},"reasoning":{"text":"The two-document path needs at least one photo document, while three non-photo documents are allowed if one is primary.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F12"]},"result":{"text":"Lee can add a third non-photo document, such as a certified school record, since the birth certificate is primary.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F24","sec01-F22"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking any two documents are enough as long as one is from the Primary Listing.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08"]},"correction":{"text":"With two documents, at least one must carry a photo; with three, all may be non-photo, but one must still be primary.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F12"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Two need a photo; three need none.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F12"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"An applicant brings two documents without photos, one from the Primary Listing. Is that bundle enough?","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F12"]},"answer":{"text":"No, because two documents need at least one photo, so a third non-photo document is needed.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F12"]},"rationale":{"text":"Three non-photo documents are accepted when one is primary, so the third document completes the bundle.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-R08"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Bringing the right papers","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F22","sec01-F24","sec01-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Identification follows set paths.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F22","sec01-F24","sec01-F15"]},{"text":"Condition and certification matter too.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F22","sec01-F24","sec01-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson is about the identification papers you bring to a license office. Alabama gives you two ways to build a bundle of documents, and each way has its own photo rule. You will also learn which documents count as primary and which count as secondary, how to prove your birth date, what a fifteen-year-old must bring, and the standards for certified and notarized papers. Many applicants are turned away not because they lack documents, but because a document is a photocopy, damaged, or improperly notarized. Knowing these rules in advance saves a second trip to the license office.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F22","sec01-F24","sec01-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Two paths to identification","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two documents, at least one with a photo.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-R08"]},{"text":"Or three documents, no photo needed.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-R08"]},{"text":"Either way, one primary document.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"For identification you can bring two documents, at least one of which has a photo. Or you can bring three documents with no photos at all. Whichever path you choose, one document must come from the Primary Listing. Transferring an out-of-state license has its own bundle: you show that license, your Social Security card or another accepted proof of the number, and one more Primary Listing document. Take Lee, who brings a certified birth certificate and a marriage license, neither with a photo. Two non-photo documents do not meet the two-document rule, so Lee needs a third document.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The photo rule trap","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F12","sec01-F22","sec01-F24"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two documents: one needs a photo.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F12","sec01-F22","sec01-F24"]},{"text":"Three documents: photos optional.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F12","sec01-F22","sec01-F24"]},{"text":"Primary item required in both.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F12","sec01-F22","sec01-F24"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. People remember that one document must be primary and forget the photo rule. On the two-document path, at least one document must bear a photo. On the three-document path, every document may be non-photo. Both paths still require one Primary Listing item. So in the worked example, Lee's certified birth certificate and marriage license fail as a pair. Adding a third non-photo document, such as a certified school record, fixes it, because three non-photo documents work when one of them is primary. When counting documents, check the number first, then the photo, then the primary item.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F12","sec01-F22","sec01-F24"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Primary and secondary lists","fact_ids":["sec01-F22","sec01-F24"]},"lines":[{"text":"Primary: birth certificate, passports, naturalization.","fact_ids":["sec01-F22","sec01-F24"]},{"text":"Secondary: marriage, military, school, court papers.","fact_ids":["sec01-F22","sec01-F24"]}],"narration":{"text":"Primary documents include a certified United States birth certificate, an unexpired United States passport, an Alabama license or ID card, a certificate of naturalization or citizenship, and a valid foreign passport together with a United States immigration document. Secondary documents include a marriage license, a military ID or form DD two fourteen, a school photo ID, a certified school record, and court decrees such as divorce, adoption or a name change. Notice that a school photo ID carries a photo but is still secondary. A photo does not make a document primary, so check which list a document is on before you rely on it.","fact_ids":["sec01-F22","sec01-F24"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Birth date and age fifteen","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F23"]},"lines":[{"text":"A prior Alabama record can prove birth date.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F23"]},{"text":"Otherwise: original or certified primary document.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F23"]},{"text":"Fifteen-year-olds show a certified birth certificate.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F23"]}],"narration":{"text":"Your birth date can be proven by a prior Alabama license or ID record. If you have no such record, only an original or certified Primary Listing document will be accepted for it. Every fifteen-year-old applicant must show a certified United States birth certificate. If the birth certificate is foreign, it must be translated into English and certified by the embassy, unless the person has a United States passport.
